content.text:
It doesn’t. Both files have `block=None`; they are single-block data.

`multiblock=True` is currently overloaded in [matplotlib.py](/home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/src/postgkyl/render/matplotlib.py:580) to mean “force all datasets onto one figure.” The example uses it only to overlay the two convergence curves.

Without it, `group_blocks()` puts each single-block dataset in a separate figure. That’s a semantic/API bug. `pg.plot(high_alpha, reference, ...)` should naturally share one figure, with actual multiblock grouping handled independently. The flag in [06_alpha_convergence.py](/home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/examples/scripts/06_alpha_convergence.py:14) should ultimately be removed after correcting that grouping behavior.
